name: lean-axiom-provenance
description: Find out what a Lean 4 project rests on and why — inherited sorry, native_decide, and which step introduced an axiom

interface.shortDescription: What your Lean proof rests on, and which step put it there
interface.longDescription: `#print axioms` says a theorem depends on Classical.choice. It does not say which step introduced it, whether the theorem's own statement required it, or whether a constructive route exists. This reports every theorem reaching a sorry anywhere upstream, everything settled by native_decide rather than the kernel, and the shortest path from any declaration to any axiom with each hop labelled a statement dependency or a proof dependency — the label being the point, since a proof edge can often be rerouted and a statement edge cannot. Also answers what breaks downstream if a definition changes, and gates CI on an unfinished proof. Works on Lean 4 and on the Metamath databases set.mm, iset.mm, nf.mm, ql.mm and hol.mm. It reads proofs the system has already checked; it proves nothing itself.
